request.system: You assist requirements analysts who apply the OGORE framework. You refine one IT goal of an organization's Initial Goal Tree Model by adapting validated goal patterns retrieved from a Goal Knowledge Base. Use only the six OGORE element types: Goal, Task, Resource, Actor, Belief, Constraint. Do not invent KPI values.

messages.content:
RETRIEVED PATTERNS:
[SKB-04/G2] (similarity 0.5308)
PATTERN SKB-04 | regional bank back office (synthetic) | financial services; zero-trust access to transaction systems
Organization goal: protect customer transactions against unauthorized access and change
IT goal G2: Every access request verified (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Requests authenticated and authorized per request (target 100%); G2-K2 Privileged sessions with multi-factor authentication (target 100%)
  Tasks: Authenticate each request against the identity provider; Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context); Require step-up authentication for privileged actions
  Resources: Identity provider; Policy decision point
  Actors: IT Security Officer; Branch Staff
  Beliefs: No network location is trusted by default
  Constraints: Shared accounts are not permitted
  Rational statement: Per-request verification removes the implicit trust that let compromised sessions move laterally.
  Conflict resolved: per-request policy checks added latency to teller screens -> cache policy decisions for 5 minutes for non-privileged reads; privileged actions always re-verified

[SKB-03/G3] (similarity 0.5206)
PATTERN SKB-03 | online retailer (synthetic) | e-commerce; customer personal data protection
Organization goal: earn customer trust by protecting personal data
IT goal G3: Data subject requests fulfilled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G3-K1 Requests closed (target within 30 days)
  Tasks: Register and verify each data subject request; Export or erase the customer's data
  Resources: Request register
  Actors: Data Protection Officer; Customer Service Agent
  Beliefs: none
  Constraints: Identity is verified before any data is released

[SKB-01/G2] (similarity 0.4802)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G2: Customer orders recorded accurately (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Order lines matching the customer purchase order (target 99.5%); G2-K2 Order confirmation sent after entry (target within 30 minutes)
  Tasks: Capture customer purchase order with price list validation; Confirm order to customer
  Resources: Customer price list; Order management module
  Actors: Sales Administrator; Customer
  Beliefs: Price lists are customer specific
  Constraints: A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-07/G2] (similarity 0.4757)
PATTERN SKB-07 | hospital pharmacy (synthetic) | medicine handling; expiry and dispensing control
Organization goal: dispense safe medicines without waste from expiry
IT goal G2: Expiry dates controlled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Items picked first-expiry-first-out (target 100%); G2-K2 Expired items removed from stock (target within 1 day of expiry)
  Tasks: Record batch and expiry at receipt; Suggest picking by earliest expiry; Report items expiring within 90 days
  Resources: Pharmacy stock module
  Actors: Pharmacist in Charge; Pharmacy Technician
  Beliefs: Regulation requires batch records for every medicine
  Constraints: Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines
  Rational statement: Batch and expiry captured at receipt make both FEFO picking and recalls possible.

QUERY:
GOAL: G05 "Access to order, stock, and contract data verified for every request (zero trust)"; parent G01 "Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure"
DOMAIN: pharmaceutical distribution to hospitals; organization type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant
KPIS: G05-K1 = Requests authenticated and authorized per request (100%); G05-K2 = Privileged actions protected by multi-factor authentication (100%); G05-K3 = Quarterly access reviews completed (100%)
ACTORS IN SCOPE: Hospital Buyer; Sales Administrator; Responsible Pharmacist; Quality Assurance Officer; IT Security Officer; Data Protection Officer; AI Product Owner
BELIEFS: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default
CONSTRAINTS: Shared accounts are not permitted

TASK: (1) Rank the retrieved patterns by relevance to the query and state why each is relevant, citing its pattern ID. (2) Adapt them to the query and propose Tasks, Actors, Resources, Beliefs, and Constraints for the goal (and sub-goals only if the goal needs further decomposition). (3) Link every proposed element to the goal ID or to one of its KPI IDs, exactly as given in the query. (4) Draft one rational statement that explains how the goal and its elements serve the parent goal and its KPIs. (5) Give, for each element, the pattern ID it was adapted from; if it was not taken from a retrieved pattern, write UNGROUNDED. Every proposed element must respect the beliefs and constraints listed in the query.

ranked_patterns.relevance: Highest relevance: SKB-04/G2 is itself a zero-trust per-request verification goal with the same two leading KPIs (per-request authentication/authorization at 100% and MFA for privileged sessions at 100%), the same belief that no network location is trusted by default, and the same no-shared-accounts constraint. Its tasks (authenticate against the identity provider, evaluate access policy per request, step-up authentication), resources (identity provider, policy decision point) and its conflict resolution (cache non-privileged read decisions for 5 minutes, always re-verify privileged actions) transfer almost directly to G05 for the order portal of a pharmaceutical distributor.

Second: SKB-03/G3 contributes the identity-verification-before-data-release constraint and the Data Protection Officer actor, which are needed because G05 governs access to customer, contract and order data that includes personal data of hospital buyers. Its 'request register' resource pattern is adaptable into the access review register required by G05-K3.

Third: SKB-01/G2 is the same order-to-cash context (distributor, customer purchase orders, price lists, order management module) and supplies the order portal/order management resource, the Sales Administrator and Customer (here Hospital Buyer) actors, and the constraint that a confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request, which defines an order-data action that G05 must treat as privileged.

Fourth: SKB-07/G2 is relevant for the regulated pharmaceutical dimension. Its constraint that only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines and its belief about regulatory batch records justify treating pharmaceutical release actions as privileged (G05-K2) and keeping auditable access records for review (G05-K3), even though its expiry-control tasks themselves do not apply.

elements.text: Non-human identities, including the LLM ordering assistant, are verified and authorized on every request like human identities
elements.justification: SKB-04/G2 verifies every access request without implicit trust; the query organization adds an LLM-based ordering assistant that issues requests to order, stock and contract data, so the goal needs one sub-goal extending per-request verification to machine identities.

elements.text: Authenticate every request to the order portal, stock and contract services against the corporate identity provider
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of the pattern task 'Authenticate each request against the identity provider' to the distributor's portal and data domains, which is what G05-K1 measures.

elements.text: Evaluate the access policy per request using role, device, context and data domain (order, stock, contract)
elements.justification: Adapts 'Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context)' and extends it with the three data domains named in G05.

elements.text: Require step-up multi-factor authentication for privileged actions such as contract price changes, credit limit changes and release of quarantined stock
elements.justification: Adapts 'Require step-up authentication for privileged actions'; the privileged action list is specialized with the pharmaceutical release action taken from SKB-07/G2 so that G05-K2 is fully covered.

elements.text: Cache policy decisions for non-privileged read requests for a short period while always re-verifying privileged actions
elements.justification: Reuses the conflict resolution of SKB-04/G2 (latency on operational screens versus per-request checks) so that portal and assistant response times stay acceptable without weakening verification of privileged actions.

elements.text: Issue a dedicated service identity to the LLM ordering assistant and restrict each assistant request to the entitlements of the authenticated end user on whose behalf it acts
elements.justification: Extension of per-request verification to the LLM assistant; required because shared accounts are not permitted, so the assistant may not run under a generic or shared credential.

elements.text: Verify the identity of the requester before releasing order, contract or personal data to a hospital buyer or an external party
elements.justification: Adapts the SKB-03/G3 practice of verifying identity before any data release, applied here to portal and assistant data disclosure.

elements.text: Perform a quarterly review and recertification of all user and service account entitlements and record the outcome
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern covers periodic recertification, but G05-K3 explicitly requires quarterly access reviews at 100%.

elements.text: Log every access decision (allow or deny) with the identity, data domain and timestamp, and use the log as evidence for the quarterly review
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-07/G2 practice of recording regulated data at the point of the transaction so that later control and traceability are possible; here decisions are recorded so reviews can be evidenced.

elements.text: Identity provider (single source of user and service identities for the portal, back office and assistant)
elements.justification: Reuse of the pattern resource 'Identity provider', extended to cover the assistant's service identity.

elements.text: Policy decision point
elements.justification: Reuse of the pattern resource 'Policy decision point', which performs the per-request authorization measured by G05-K1.

elements.text: Multi-factor and step-up authentication service
elements.justification: Implied by the pattern's step-up authentication task and its MFA KPI; made explicit as the resource that enables G05-K2.

elements.text: Access review register recording entitlements, reviewers and decisions per quarter
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-03/G3 'Request register' resource, repurposed as the register that evidences completion of quarterly access reviews.

elements.text: Order portal and order management module as the protected systems holding order, stock and contract data
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-01/G2 'Order management module' and 'Customer price list' resources, which in this organization hold the contract and order data that G05 protects.

elements.text: IT Security Officer (owner of access policy, identity provider and the verification controls)
elements.justification: Same accountable actor as in the zero-trust pattern and listed in the query scope.

elements.text: Sales Administrator (internal user of order and contract data, subject to per-request verification)
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-01/G2 Sales Administrator and from the pattern's internal staff role verified on each request.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer (external portal user whose requests are authenticated and authorized individually)
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-01/G2 'Customer' actor and the SKB-04/G2 verified end user, applied to the hospital customer of this distributor.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist (approver of privileged pharmaceutical actions requiring step-up authentication)
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-07/G2 'Pharmacist in Charge' who alone may release quarantined medicines; such releases are privileged actions under G05-K2.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer (verifies that identity checks and data access rules protect personal data)
elements.justification: Taken from SKB-03/G3 where the DPO owns identity verification before data release.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer (reviewer of access rights to regulated order and batch-related data in the quarterly review)
elements.justification: Adapted from the regulated-control role in SKB-07/G2; in the query scope QA owns regulatory evidence, which fits the quarterly review KPI.

elements.text: AI Product Owner (accountable for the LLM assistant's service identity and its scoped entitlements)
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern includes an AI component; the actor is in the query scope and is needed to own the assistant's identity and entitlements.

elements.text: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default
elements.justification: The pattern belief 'No network location is trusted by default' matches the query belief and justifies per-request verification.

elements.text: The LLM ordering assistant holds no entitlements of its own; it only acts within the rights of the authenticated user it serves
elements.justification: Needed to apply zero-trust reasoning to the assistant; not present in any retrieved pattern but consistent with the no-shared-accounts constraint.

elements.text: Regulation requires traceable records of who accessed and changed regulated order, batch and contract data
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-07/G2 belief that regulation requires batch records, extended to access traceability that underpins quarterly reviews.

elements.text: Shared accounts are not permitted for users, administrators or the LLM assistant
elements.justification: Query constraint identical to the pattern constraint, extended to the machine identity so every request is attributable.

elements.text: Identity is verified before any order, contract or personal data is released
elements.justification: Direct reuse of the SKB-03/G3 constraint, which supports the per-request authorization KPI.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist may authorize release of quarantined medicines, and only after step-up multi-factor authentication
elements.justification: Combines the SKB-07/G2 release constraint with the SKB-04/G2 step-up requirement so that the regulated action is covered by G05-K2.

elements.text: A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request, and such edits are treated as privileged actions
elements.justification: Reuses the SKB-01/G2 constraint and classifies post-confirmation edits as privileged, which brings them under the MFA KPI.

output.rational_statement: Parent goal G01 requires the regulated order-to-delivery chain to be both controlled and secure, which only holds if every request for order, stock or contract data is attributable and authorized, whether it comes from a hospital buyer in the portal, a sales administrator in the back office, or the LLM ordering assistant. G05 therefore removes implicit trust in the network: authenticating each request at the identity provider and evaluating policy per request at the policy decision point delivers G05-K1; step-up multi-factor authentication on privileged actions such as contract price changes, post-confirmation order edits and release of quarantined stock delivers G05-K2; and quarterly entitlement recertification supported by the access review register and the access decision log delivers G05-K3 and the regulatory evidence QA and the DPO need. Caching decisions only for non-privileged reads while always re-verifying privileged actions keeps portal and assistant response times acceptable without weakening control, and the no-shared-accounts constraint plus a dedicated, user-scoped service identity for the assistant ensure that every action affecting a regulated delivery can be traced to one accountable identity.
